summary: Iter26 — Hybrid PDF Storage (P2). Tested backend retention sweep + admin endpoints + RBAC + frontend StorageCard. Existing /app/backend/tests/test_pdf_retention.py PASSES (seeds old+fresh GridFS blobs, verifies only old purges, session pointer cleared, days=0 no-op). New /app/backend/tests/test_iter26_pdf_storage_endpoints.py: 9/11 PASS — founder happy paths, support agent allowed for read+default purge, support agent BLOCKED from days override (403), invalid days=400, unauth blocked (401/403), regression on /system/data-health (overall + auto_incidents_opened still present). FRONTEND: System Health page renders Storage card with all 3 KPI tiles (TOTAL STORED, ELIGIBLE FOR SWEEP, RETENTION WINDOW), session_reports row carries 'AUTO-PURGE 30D' pill, image buckets show PERMANENT, Refresh button triggers GET /api/admin/v2/system/storage. APScheduler boot log mentions pdf_retention_sweep_0315_ist (visible in supervisor backend logs). Daily 03:15 IST job not directly invoked but path is unit-tested.

critical.issue: Tenant-scoped super_admin (admin@delhi.test, role=super_admin at clinic-delhi-test) can read platform GridFS storage stats AND trigger a real PDF purge across the entire platform. Got 200 instead of expected 403. Cause: utils/rbac.py:require_permission() short-circuits ANY user with role in {founder, super_admin} regardless of clinic_id — there is no platform vs tenant distinction. Per review request these tenant users 'must 403'. This is a cross-tenant privilege-escalation concern: a Delhi clinic super_admin should never purge Mumbai/ACS audiogram PDFs.

minor.issue: Endpoint signature uses `payload: dict | None = None`. FastAPI will treat this as a query/body free-form param and skip Pydantic validation; works today but is brittle. Suggest a small `PurgeReq(BaseModel)` with optional days:int.

Image buckets (clinic_logos, user_signatures, user_avatars, transfer_signatures) are hard-coded inside services/pdf_retention.py. If new GridFS buckets are added later they won't show on the dashboard. Consider listing all *.files collections via db.list_collection_names().

issues: On 1440x900 the Storage card lands fully below the fold — fine for founder workflows but worth noting for screenshot tours.
Recharts width(-1) console warnings repeat on every render of the System Health page (not Storage-specific, pre-existing) — chart container has a 0-height parent during layout.

action_items: Decide & enforce platform-vs-tenant separation for /api/admin/v2/* endpoints. Easiest fix: in admin_panel_b.py guards, require `user['clinic_id'] == platform_clinic_id` (or a `is_platform_admin` flag) in addition to require_permission('system:read'). This will make admin@delhi.test 403 as the spec demands without breaking founder/admin@acs.in.
Optional: tighten payload typing on /system/storage/purge-pdfs with a Pydantic model.
Optional: auto-discover GridFS buckets in gridfs_storage_stats() instead of hard-coding.

rca of the issue: The /admin/v2/* router enforces RBAC purely via require_permission() which delegates to utils/rbac.py. That helper short-circuits when user.role in {founder, super_admin} — it never checks user.clinic_id. Because admin@delhi.test is seeded as role=super_admin at clinic-delhi-test, they bypass every permission gate including platform-only endpoints like /system/storage. Reproduction: login as admin@delhi.test → GET /api/admin/v2/system/storage → 200 OK with full bucket listing. Mitigation: add a platform gate (e.g. require user.clinic_id == os.environ['PLATFORM_CLINIC_ID'] || 'clinic-platform-audinexa') inside require_permission OR introduce require_platform_admin() and use it on every /admin/v2/* router endpoint that exposes platform-wide data.
